subject: Processor change notification: TerraCard routing relay addition - evidence & canary plan
messages:
From: Marcus Li <marcus.li@terracard.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@terracard.com
Date: Tue, 25 Sep 2028 15:08:00 -0400
Subject: Notice: addition of ‘EdgeRelayX’ to routing processors - immediate info needed

Hannah,

We were notified this morning that Redwood plans to route a subset of TerraCard-bound requests via a new transit/relay provider (internal name ‘EdgeRelayX’). Before we can approve any routing change that affects TerraCard data, our security and procurement teams need:

- A current, downloadable list of all subprocessors that will touch TerraCard data (including IP ranges and countries of operation).
- A short dataflow diagram or description of what data is sent to EdgeRelayX and the retention/processing purpose.
- Evidence of encryption in transit (TLS versions/ciphers) and any KMS or HSM involvement.
- SOC2/ISO attestation or an equivalent security summary for EdgeRelayX (if available).
- Proposed canary rollout plan and monitoring signals to guarantee no customer-impacting regressions.

Can you send the subprocessor roster and the DPA addendum that covers temporary relays? We are on a tight change freeze but can review an evidence bundle quickly if provided. Ideally we’d have this by EOD Thursday so procurement can triage.

Thanks,
Marcus Li
Sr. Security Manager, TerraCard
Marcus.li@terracard.com
[Attachment: terra_request_template.xlsx]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Li <marcus.li@terracard.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of ‘EdgeRelayX’ to routing processors - immediate info needed

Marcus — thanks for the heads up and the checklist. We pulled together the materials you asked for and attached the current roster and a draft DPA addendum that explicitly calls out transient relays. Key points up front:

- Who/where: EdgeRelayX is a transit relay subcontractor operated by RelayWorks Ltd. Processing locations: US (primary), UK (failover).
- Data types: only routing metadata and request/response byte streams necessary for delivery; we do not persist PII beyond short-lived buffers used for in-flight delivery.
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 enforced end-to-end; we use AWS KMS for ephemeral key wrapping on dedicated on-prem pockets where applicable.

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessors_2028-09.csv (full roster), dpa-addendum-v2.pdf (draft addendum).

Proposed near-term timeline:
- Thu 2028-09-28: TerraCard legal/security reviews DPA addendum and roster (requested).
- Mon 2028-10-02: 10% canary traffic for 48 hours (if approved).
- Rollout escalation: immediate rollback to direct routing on any elevated error-rate or latency regression beyond agreed SLO delta.

Marissa is copied to own the canary monitoring hooks and kimberly will lead any procurement/redline coordination. If it helps, I can package a short evidence zip (SOC summary + network diagrams) by EOD today.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_2028-09.csv]
[Attachment: dpa-addendum-v2.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Li <marcus.li@terracard.com>, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Sep 2028 11:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of ‘EdgeRelayX’ to routing processors - actionable canary plan

Marcus — quick follow-up from ops/monitoring side with specifics for the canary we propose:

Canary plan (proposed):
- Stage 1 (10% traffic, 48 hours): real traffic mirrored but routed to EdgeRelayX for 10% of eligible requests. No persistence beyond ephemeral buffers.
- Stage 2 (50% traffic, 72 hours): increase if Stage 1 metrics are stable.
- Fallback: automatic reroute to prior path and cancellation of roll forward if:
  - error-rate increases > 1.5x baseline for 10 consecutive minutes, or
  - median p95 latency increases by > 150ms, or
  - any unauthorised data residency access is detected.

Monitoring signals we will provide to TerraCard (dashboards):
- per-route error rate, p50/p95 latency, tokenization/response-consistency regressions, and a small alerting window for anomalous egress destinations.

Procurement/legal ask: please review the attached DPA addendum and sign via DocuSign link we will provide once you confirm the go/no-go window. Kimberley/kimberly_park is assigned to manage redlines — kimberly, please confirm you’ll own contract turnaround (target: 48 business hours).

I’m also attaching a short markdown canary-rollout-plan.md with the checks we’ll run during each milestone.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: canary-rollout-plan.md]

From: Marcus Li <marcus.li@terracard.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@terracard.com
Date: Fri, 29 Sep 2028 10:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of ‘EdgeRelayX’ to routing processors - actionable canary plan

Thanks, Hannah and Marissa — that level of detail helps. TerraCard can proceed on the following basis:

- We will review the DPA addendum and roster today. Legal asked for one small redline on the SLA-exception window; kimberly_park, I’ll route that to you directly.
- We require a KMS attestation from RelayWorks (or confirmation that Redwood’s KMS policy covers ephemeral wrapping) before Stage 2.
- Approved canary: 10% traffic starting Mon 2028-10-02 for 48 hours, subject to immediate shutdown if the monitoring thresholds you described are tripped.

Please send the DocuSign link when the addendum is finalized. Also — for our records, please include a short evidence package with the SOC summary and the transit network diagram (attachments accepted as zipped bundle). If you can deliver that by EOD today, procurement will sign off faster.

Marcus Li
Sr. Security Manager, TerraCard
Marcus.li@terracard.com
[Preferred reply: include attestation and DocuSign link as separate items]
